p: California buyers have usually tried AI already. The question is less often whether to use it and more often why the pilot never reached the rest of the company, or why the bill for tools keeps rising while the work looks the same.

Bay Area companies are more often software, SaaS, AI and life sciences firms that want AI features in the product, clean data and a cloud setup that does not burn cash.

sections.h: CCPA and CPRA from day one
p: The California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act, gives Californians the right to know, delete and correct their personal data, to opt out of its sale or sharing, and to limit how sensitive personal information is used. The California Privacy Protection Agency and the Attorney General both enforce it, and newer regulations add duties around risk assessments and automated decision-making technology that phase in over the next few years.

For AI projects that means a few practical habits. We keep a record of what personal data each tool sees, avoid sending sensitive data to services that do not need it, set retention limits, and make sure opt-outs reach every system, including ad platforms. Where a tool makes or supports significant decisions about people, we design human review in. Your counsel has the final say on compliance.

California projects start with a 15-minute call and a short discovery, followed by a written roadmap in 5 to 7 days. After that, one shared channel holds updates, decisions and files, and review calls are booked at times that suit your team. Every date we agree goes in writing, so you always know what is due next.
When the project needs it, such as a leadership workshop or a shoot, we come on site. Otherwise everything runs through video calls, a shared plan and a weekly written update.

We have run and broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events, and the lesson carries into every AI rollout: the date does not move. Launches, board reviews and campaign deadlines get the same treatment, planned backwards and agreed in writing.

California has no shortage of AI specialists, so our case rests on range. One team covers AI, cloud and data, and also the marketing, video, animation and 3D that turn a new capability into customers. You get one Signal Lead, specialist teams behind them, and a process of Talk, Plan, Build, Grow.
Cost depends on scope: the number of use cases, the data and systems involved, privacy and security requirements, the creative volume if marketing is included, and whether you want ongoing support.

faqs.q: What should we prepare before the first call?
faqs.a: Very little. A short note on the process you want to improve, the tools your California team uses today and any AI pilots you have already tried is enough. On the call we ask about goals and constraints, and if there is a fit we follow up with a discovery plan and dates in writing. We come on site when the project needs it, for example for a workshop or a production day.

faqs.q: How do you handle CCPA and CPRA in AI projects?
faqs.a: We document what personal data each AI tool processes, keep sensitive data out of tools that do not need it, set retention limits and make sure opt-out and deletion requests reach every connected system. Where AI supports decisions about people, we add human review. Your counsel reviews and approves the setup.

faqs.q: Our AI pilot worked but never rolled out. Can you help?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a common starting point. We review why it stalled, usually data access, unclear ownership, missing evaluation or security concerns, fix those, and plan a staged rollout with measures agreed up front. Sometimes the honest answer is to buy a tool instead, and we will say so.

faqs.q: Do you work with entertainment and media companies in Los Angeles?
faqs.a: Yes. Our video, motion, AI video and 3D teams sit alongside our AI and data teams, so we can automate parts of a production or content workflow and also produce the content. We have run and broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events, so live deadlines are familiar territory.

faqs.q: Can you build AI features for a San Francisco SaaS product?
faqs.a: Yes. We build agents, retrieval over documents and other AI features inside your product, working in your repositories with code review and evaluation. We can also handle the cloud, data and launch marketing, so the feature reaches users with a plan behind it.

faqs.q: What does AI consulting cost in California?
faqs.a: It depends on scope. The main factors are the number of use cases, the systems and data involved, privacy and security requirements, and whether marketing or ongoing support is included. After a 15-minute call we send a written scope with dates.
